name: Automatic lowering of linear PureScript expressions
description: An extra TAST-to-arrow compiler makes explicit routing unnecessary in a restricted source language.

cases.reason: Ordinary PureScript function and let bindings, before extra linear checking.
Two resources and a reversed result pair, before routing is generated.
Carry a native owner and before/after snapshots through mutation.
A single-use alias must not create a new resource.
Lexical shadowing requires binding identity, not names alone.
Duplication of a shareable scalar is explicit.
Ordinary PureScript permits implicit scalar duplication; this restricted linear compiler does not yet insert it.
Ordinary types alone allow duplicate resource consumption; the added pass must reject it.
Ordinary PureScript permits discarding a resource; this strict linear fragment requires use.
A native borrowing API still needs a separate ownership-threading transformation.
The native lowering is first-order even though the separate BCI algorithm tests higher-order terms.
The generated programs use the previously tested generic native arrow interpreter.
